findings.title: Materials' 100% growth bet is extreme
findings.body: Materials shows a 46-point percentile gap between its trailing and forward lenses, with the forward multiple at the 14th percentile while trailing sits at the 60th. The market is underwriting a 100 percent earnings jump, a level of optimism that appears disconnected from the sector's own five-year history.

findings.title: Health Care's 44% compression defies its percentile
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple has dropped 19 percentile points in both the past week and month, yet still sits at the 81st percentile. The 44 percent compression between trailing and forward earnings implies an 80 percent growth surge, a bet that seems unusually aggressive for a sector already priced near its five-year peak.

findings.title: Utilities' forward price ignores trailing reality
findings.body: Utilities trades at the 23rd percentile on a forward basis but at the 1st percentile on trailing earnings, a 22-point gap. The forward multiple is barely cheaper than trailing, implying just 4 percent growth, which suggests the market is not rewarding the sector's cheap trailing valuation at all.
